title: two friends agree to share, and then they play Doom
summary: LAN party mode. Until now every player was a stranger to every other: your namespace was a closed room. Now two friends can both say yes, and only then do their rooms open to each other, on the one port a game needs and nothing else. To show that something real crosses it, the release ships a Doom match: alice runs an Odamex server with Freedoom, bob's automated client joins through the party, runs and shoots for 40 seconds, and alice's server log is the witness. Without the party, or after bob leaves, the same client gets no answer: those red lines are the fence working.

player.title: Players 1 and 2: alice and bob, two friends
steps: Both of them got a place the usual way and have a namespace of their own. Nothing of alice's reaches bob, and nothing of bob's reaches alice.
Alice runs a Doom deathmatch server in her namespace: Odamex with Freedoom, the free game data, on one UDP port. Her own robot joins it (her namespace: no party needed).
Bob's client, a pod in his namespace, tries it. Nobody answers: the line marked '# expected' is the fence, not a failure.
Alice invites bob. One yes is not a party: the client still gets nothing.
Bob accepts. Now both said yes, and the host's next tick opens the one port the game needs, both ways.
Bob's client joins through the party, sees the map, runs and shoots for 40 seconds and quits, in the same match as alice's robot. The GIF below is his screen.
Bob leaves the party. The same client, the same server: nobody answers again.

host.title: Player 3: the host who runs the pool
steps: The tick admits both friends. The host never joins their game.
When the second yes arrives, the tick opens the party: only that port, only between those two namespaces.
Alice's server log is the witness: who connected, who joined the game, how long he stayed, with each one's frags and deaths on one line.
A reconcile run twice says unchanged. When bob leaves, the next tick closes it and nothing is left behind.

casts.title: alice's and bob's screens
casts.caption: a real make showcase-doom run (poc-doom) in Incus VMs with Cilium. The three 'no server answered' lines are the point (before any yes, after one yes, after bob leaves) and each one is marked '# expected'.

casts.title: The host's screen
casts.caption: the tick that admits them, the party that opens, and alice's server log: alice and bob connected, joined the game, stayed, left, each with frags and deaths. No errors here.

media.title: bob's screen during the match
media.alt: A first-person view of a Freedoom level: a marine runs down a corridor firing a pistol, with the health and ammo bar of Doom at the bottom.
media.caption: captured by the automated client under a virtual screen (Xvfb + ffmpeg) while it played alice's server through the party: 320x200, 24 seconds of the 40 it played.

features.name: A party needs both
features.what: edge-mesh party invite and accept: each friend writes a consent in their own namespace; the host opens a pair of NetworkPolicies only when both exist, on the ports both named within the host's list, and nobody else.
features.why: You can say yes to a friend without opening your room to strangers, and nobody can say it for you.
features.command:
sudo edge-mesh party invite bob
sudo edge-mesh party accept alice
make poc-party   # PY01-PY17

features.name: A Doom match over a party
features.what: alice's Odamex server (Freedoom, 10666/UDP) and bob's automated client play through the party, across two nodes over Nebula, on Cilium. The server log, not the client, is the proof; before the party and after leave nothing connects.
features.why: A party is only worth having if something real crosses it, and a game is the plainest test of UDP over the mesh.
features.command:
make poc-doom      # DM01-DM16
make showcase-doom RELEASE=v0.3.0-poc

features.name: Nothing non-free, nothing pulled
features.what: The image has Odamex (GPL-2.0-or-later) and Freedoom (BSD-3-Clause) only: no doom.wad, no doom2.wad, both licences inside. It is built once from a Debian base pinned by digest and sources pinned by SHA-256, and loaded into the two nodes: no registry, no pull.
features.why: A joined stranger's node pulls nothing from anywhere, and the demo cannot ship what it has no right to.

features.name: A server that stays between friends
features.what: The Doom server does not announce itself to the public master servers (sv_usemasters 0); its address stays inside the party.
features.why: A game server that phones the internet would tell the world where it runs.
features.command: sudo edge-mesh kubectl exec doom-server -- grep Masters /tmp/server.log

features.name: Game screens on this page
features.what: A release can show a GIF of a real run next to its terminal recordings. It is an image of this server only, so the page's CSP did not change, and the test that scans every recording for leaks scans the GIF too.
features.why: Some things are easier to believe when you see them.
features.command:
make showcase-doom RELEASE=v0.3.0-poc
python3 -m unittest poc.test_whatsnew
